According to recent polling averages, Democrats lead Republicans by 6 to 7 points on the generic congressional ballot as of late August 2026. An Emerson College poll released in mid-August showed 51% support for Democratic candidates compared to 43% for Republicans, with 6% undecided. Ballotpedia’s polling index as of August 26 put Democrats ahead by 7 points, while Nate Silver’s tracking showed a Democratic margin of 6.6 points. results.title: Midterm election 2026 set for November with Democrats leading in polls

results.content:
Right now, Democrats have a wave-sized lead on the generic ballot: about 6 or 7 percentage points, on average. They probably won't reprise 2018 and flip 41 House seats again in November, in part because red-state Republican lawmakers have recently redrawn congressional maps across the South to benefit their party in ways that blue-state Democrats have been unable to keep up with. But they only need to pick up three seats to win back the House.
